neighbours.label: Final piece of a premodified content noun phrase (adjective/noun compound, possessive + noun, or multi-piece name) that has just opened a clause after a lead-in, as subject, small-clause subject after 'makes', or copula complement after 'that's/it's', in punchy editorial or marketing copy, before the predicate arrives; the same NP as an object, a pronoun subject, or a bare 'the X of Y' subject stays quiet.
fire: By the time dessert arrives, the bill here makes airport sushi seem almost reasonable.
Honestly, this new lens makes smartphone photography look almost professional.
Whatever the weather throws at you, your hiking boots will stay bone dry.
On a cold morning, your car battery may not have much left to give.
Say what you want about the prices, but that's customer service done right.
Coming to you live from a cantina in Mos Eisley, it's Tatooine Tonight!
Seven posture tips your lower back will thank you for.
Mark my words, facial recognition is coming to every airport.
quiet: After a week in Tokyo, don't bother complaining about airport sushi.
Even five years ago, you never expected this much from smartphone photography.
No matter what the weather does, keep the mud off your hiking boots.
After consulting the industry, the national transport agency published revised guidance on car battery disposal.
Whatever you think of the prices, they built this place on customer service.
Live from a dusty cantina on the edge of town, we bring you the best music on Tatooine!
After a long day at the desk, try these five stretches for your lower back.
With a fingerprint on every phone, the age of passwords is drawing to a close.

predictions: 6-8/8 fires >= 0.20. The two 'makes X seem/look' small-clause items (airport sushi, smartphone photography; subjects 'the bill'/'this new lens' cannot produce the NP, forcing the small-clause reading) and the two fronted-adverbial possessive subjects (hiking boots, car battery) ~0.4-0.7; 'that's customer service' ~0.35-0.5; 'it's Tatooine' ~0.25-0.45 with the peak on 'ine' (or on 'ley'/the comma closing 'Mos Eisley'); the headline 'your lower back' and plain-subject 'facial recognition' items are coin flips at 0.1-0.3 (modeled on 0.241/0.212); median fire ~0.4. Near misses: three imperative/object-position items (airport sushi, hiking boots, lower back) <= 0.08; the they/we pronoun subjects (customer service, Tatooine) <= 0.10; 'the age of passwords' ~0.10; two designated risks: 'Even five years ago, you never expected' (pronoun 'you' right after a fronted-adverbial comma; corpus ', you are' hit 0.88 of max vs probe 0.064) ~0.05-0.3, and the dry 'the national transport agency' subject (register test) ~0.1-0.4. Expect 0-1 near miss >= 0.30, AUROC ~0.92; if both risks leak, the label's pronoun exclusion or register qualifier is falsified and that is the result.
notes: Probes split on left context up to the NP head.
